name: The nobles who exacted usury of their brethren
charge: Lending on interest; taking brethren's lands and children for debt
summary: During the rebuilding of the wall, the poor cried out that they had mortgaged their fields and vineyards and sold their sons and daughters into bondage to pay the king's tribute and the nobles' interest. Nehemiah was very angry and set a great assembly against the nobles and rulers.
offense: Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. The law forbids taking usury from a poor brother or holding him as a bondservant; Nehemiah adds that they were buying back Jews sold to the heathen while their own class was selling them again.
judgment: Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money. They said, we will restore them, and swore before the priests. Nehemiah shook his lap: so God shake out every man that performeth not this promise.
